findings.text: _head_blob_bytes duplicates the capability reckon/crew/routing.py:981 _git_blob already owns: both run git against a revision:path in byte mode and return None on a non-zero exit. The module already imports several privates from reckon.crew.routing (_git, _git_blob's sibling _boundary_tree_roots), so the owner was reachable; the addition neither extends nor wraps it. git show HEAD:<path> used by the owner also reads the object store without taking the index lock, so the plumbing-vs-porcelain distinction the docstring draws is not load-bearing here.

_restore_landing_writes's docstring still states "a tracked path whose restore is refused keeps its working-tree write — the retry commits that write, so taking it back would discard the recorded comment." That is the design this node reversed: _restore_tracked_landing_write (line 1748) now takes the write back by rewriting the working tree from HEAD's blob. The paragraph above the changed function is now stale and contradicts the code beneath it, so a reader trusts a rationale the node deliberately removed.
